newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa retail sales growth seen slackening in Q3.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa retail sales growth seen slackening in Q3.

text.p: Third-quarter retail sales growth is expected to slow after gaining momentum in the second quarter, the University of Stellenbosch's Bureau for Economic Research (BER) said on Monday.
"Retailers surveyed expect the volume of total sales to increase (in the third quarter) albeit, at a much lower rate than during the second quarter," BER said in its latest retail survey.
Semi-durable sales were expected to remain flat, non-durable sales were seen shrinking further and durable sales were forecast to rise at a lower rate.
"The expected slackening in sales volumes could be one reason why respondents expect a lower rate of increase in average selling prices," BER said.
Though average purchase prices were expected to pick up, retailers said they planned to absorb some of the cost increases. That could pressure profit margins.
It said second-quarter business confidence in the retail sector improved slightly but remained at a relatively low level.
Orders increased at a lower pace than sales, probably because retailers cut stocks instead of ordering more from wholesalers and manufacturers.
BER said consumer confidence appeared to be strengthening and could pave the way for a private consumption spending recovery towards year end.
In the wholesale trade, growth tapered off in the second quarter and business confidence was dented. Respondents expected conditions to deteriorate further in the third quarter.
New and used vehicle sales fell in the second quarter, but motor dealers were reasonably optimistic about new car sales in the third quarter although stocks were still expected to outstrip demand.
